# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Healthy Blue Louisiana — Member Appeals
*Please send this to the appeal address printed on the denial letter, or call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.*

**From:** Taylor Ellison
**Member ID:** W398278970
**Plan:** Healthy Blue Louisiana (Commercial/ACA), State of Louisiana

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-02 — Reference number POC-19407106E9-21880 — Total hip replacement, CPT 27130**

**Governing policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130). The notice dated 2026-08-02 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery. My surgeon, Duval, MD, submitted this request and documented in my records why the procedure is needed.

The notice did not tell me which specific criterion my records were found not to meet. I am writing to show, point by point, that the records already submitted line up with the plan's own published language. My appeal must be received by 2027-01-29, and I am submitting it well within that period.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. Length of conservative treatment.**

The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, modified Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3)"

My records show 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, from 2026-02-28 to 2026-06-06, with 24 visits completed, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Fourteen weeks is more than the twelve weeks the plan's own language calls for.

**2. What conservative treatment has to include.**

The guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

I completed physical therapy, and I also had two other treatments: NSAIDs for 8 months, which did not give me adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-08, which gave me only about 4 weeks of partial relief. That is physical therapy plus more than one complementary strategy.

**3. Completing the full course, and what happened afterward.**

The guideline states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

and

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

I finished the full course of therapy. My pain has been progressive over 12 months and is not relieved by rest. The injection relief lasted about four weeks and then ended. I have not significantly improved.

**4. Documentation in the clinical notes.**

The guideline states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

and

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

The packet contains all of these elements: symptom duration (12 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest); my specific functional limitations; and the type and duration of each treatment (physical therapy 2026-02-28 to 2026-06-06 with 24 visits, NSAIDs for 8 months, injection on 2026-03-08). The 24 completed visits and the discharge note show my compliance with the plan of therapy.

**5. Pain and functional impairment.**

The guideline states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I walk with a cane, that I am limited to about one block, and that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted. Those are daily activities I can no longer do on my own. If the reviewer needs the numeric pain score to complete this element, it is in my treating records: [numeric pain rating as recorded in the clinical notes, if documented — my office can supply this].

**6. Functional limitation and physical exam.**

The guideline states:

> "Functional limitation secondary to hip pathology which interferes with the ability to perform age - appropriate daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or Tönnis grade 3)"

and

> "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic hip arthritis (e.g., pain with passive motion of the hip, antalgic gait, limited motion) unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, diffuse modified Outerbridge grade 4, or Tonnis grade 3"

The limitations above — cane, one block, shoes — are exactly the kind of age-appropriate daily activities the policy describes. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, which matches the examples of limited motion and pain on motion in the plan's own text.

**7. Imaging.**

The guideline states:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods:"

and

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis , or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph was taken on 2026-07-06, which is within the past 12 months. The report describes joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes — that is, it notes the degree of joint space narrowing and describes the specific findings the plan's language asks the report to address.

I want to be straightforward about one point. The guideline elsewhere refers to grading scales, in this language:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as Tönnis grade 3, diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV, or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4"

My radiology report describes the findings themselves rather than assigning a grade. If the denial rests on the absence of a stated grade, I ask that the plan say so directly, so my surgeon can provide a graded read of the same 2026-07-06 study rather than have the request closed on a documentation point.

## Two things I am asking the plan to clarify

First, the excerpts of this guideline that I have — including the criterion that reads "Joint damage or destruction due to osteoarthritis, inflammatory disease or other chronic condition when ALL the following requirements have been met:" and the imaging criterion quoted above — end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not able to address requirements I have not been shown.

Second, the guideline also lists other qualifying indications, such as "Hip fracture or complications including malunion, nonunion, or failed prior fixation," "Primary and secondary tumors of the proximal femur, acetabulum, or pelvis," and "Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) with unresponsive severe pain." I do not know which pathway the reviewer applied to my case.

So that this appeal can be decided on the merits, I ask the plan to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria my request was found not to meet, and the specific document relied on.

## What I am requesting

I ask that Healthy Blue Louisiana overturn the determination dated 2026-08-02 (reference POC-19407106E9-21880) and authorize total hip replacement, CPT 27130. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation identifying the exact criterion not met and the evidence relied on, the reviewer's name and specialty, a free copy of all documents used in the review, and information on my next level of appeal, including external review.

I have included: the denial notice, the physical therapy discharge note, the 2026-07-06 radiograph report, and my surgeon's clinical notes. Please contact me if anything further would help.

Thank you for taking another look at this. Walking one block with a cane and needing help with my shoes is not where I expected to be, and my surgeon and I both believe this surgery is the right next step.

---

**Sincerely,**

Taylor Ellison
